issue_title: Under-escalation when ground-truth severity is 2 (high risk)

issue_summary.title: Escalation flag not consistently set to true on GT=2 cases
issue_summary.overview: When the ground-truth label indicates imminent risk (severity 2), the assistant should set escalate=true. However, summary metrics show under-escalation: rate_when_gt_2 is ~0.70–0.74 across reasoning levels (minimal: 0.722, low: 0.714, medium: 0.737, high: 0.701). This means 26–30% of high-risk conversations are not flagged for escalation.
issue_summary.desired_behavior: For any conversation with high-risk signals (severity 2), the model should explicitly set escalate=true and call the assessment tool.
issue_summary.observed_behavior: In many GT=2 cases, escalate is missing or false. Even where severity is predicted correctly (pred=2), the escalate rate is not 100% (e.g., rate_when_gt_2_and_pred_2 is ~0.98–0.99, leaving misses).
issue_summary.self_assessed_severity_justification: Potential safety miss in crisis scenarios; mitigated somewhat by high tool-call rate and near-100% escalate when pred=2.
issue_summary.self_assessed_breadth_justification: Affects a specific subset (GT=2) across the dataset.

steps_to_reproduce: Run eval.ipynb to generate the latest summary.
Inspect eval_summary_*.json for the 'escalation.rate_when_gt_2' metric per reasoning level.
Optionally, examine cases in eval_details_*/details_*.csv where gt_severity==2 but escalate_pred==false or escalate_present==false.
notes: Metrics source: eval_summary_20250814T175832Z.json. rate_when_gt_2: minimal=0.7216, low=0.7139, medium=0.7371, high=0.7010. rate_when_gt_2_and_pred_2 ~0.982–0.986 indicates near-perfect escalate when the model also predicts severity 2, pointing to misses mainly when the model under-predicts severity.
